page: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, providing 3686 GB of capacity with Premium Storage capability, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

In benchmark testing, the E96ads_v5 demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU encryption. Memory subsystem performance is also notable, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top 10% and small-block read-only memory bandwidth placing in the top 25% at 6081.25 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths fall into the middle 50% average tier. Single-core performance, measured via Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, consistently registers in the average to strong ranges.

The combination of high memory capacity, substantial local NVMe storage, and strong multi-threaded execution makes this server suitable for memory-intensive database operations, large-scale data processing, and enterprise applications. Passmark database operations and Redis SET benchmarks both rank in the top 25%, confirming its efficiency for transactional workloads. While it lacks GPU acceleration, limiting its utility for heavy deep learning training, it achieves strong performance in CPU-based LLM text generation for small and medium models.

It delivers 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores running at 3.7 GHz, paired with 672.0 GB of RAM and 3686 GB of local storage. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance achieves top-tier multi-core CPU performance and encryption capabilities, ranking in the top 10% of benchmarks. Its memory subsystem also scores in the top tier, supported by strong database and Redis transaction throughput. While single-core speeds and large-block memory bandwidth remain in the average tier, the server's high resource density and local storage capacity make it highly efficient for memory-intensive enterprise databases, large-scale data processing, and multi-threaded workloads.
